text:
B: Alright! Can you hear me?
A: Yes, I can hear you. Can you hear me alright? Sorry, I always ask that.
B: Loud and clear. I'm Darren. One of the two Darrens, you might've heard.
A: Leanne. Yes, I've just had the other one, actually. He said you'd both had a very similar sort of call.
B: Ha, we did. Same town, same dogs, near enough. Where are you, then?
A: Walsall.
B: Walsall! That's two of you, then. I had Kelly before, she's Walsall as well.
A: Oh, Ellie mentioned a Kelly. I don't know her, though. It's bigger than people think, Walsall.
B: Fair enough. What d'you do?
A: I'm a practice nurse at a GP surgery. Erm, asthma clinics, diabetes reviews, smears, baby jabs. That sort of thing.
B: Oh, you're the one with the needle. My mum's always on about her nurse. She's late seventies, down in Bridgwater, and she's starting to struggle a bit, to be honest. Getting an appointment's like winning the lottery, she reckons.
A: Yes, sorry, it probably is. Our phone lines on a Monday morning are a nightmare, I'll be honest. Is she managing alright? You don't have to say.
B: No, you're alright. She's okay, she's just slowing down. Bit forgetful, bit wobbly on her feet. My brother's in Weston, I'm in Taunton, and neither of us has really sat down and worked out who does what. We talk about the football instead. Classic blokes.
A: I think a lot of families are like that, you know. It's hard to start that conversation. Sometimes it helps if the surgery knows, though, if she's got someone they can ring.
B: That's a good shout, actually. I'll mention it to her. Anyway, cheerful stuff. What d'you do when you're not jabbing people?
A: Oh, not much, really. I walk along the canal most evenings. I read a lot, crime novels. And I feed next door's cat when they're away. He's called Biscuit, he sits on my wheelie bin.
B: You're joking. Biscuit?
A: Yes. Why, is that funny?
B: My dog's called Biscuit. And Ellie's dog's called Biscuit. That's three Biscuits in one group.
A: Oh, that's lovely. Well, Biscuit's not mine, I just borrow him. I don't think he'd get on with a terrier.
B: Ha, no, he'd have him up a tree. Do you get away much?
A: Erm, once a year, usually. I go to Tenby, or North Norfolk sometimes. Sometimes with my mom. I'm not very good with airports, so I stick to places I can drive to.
B: Tenby! We do Pembrokeshire with the dog a couple of times a year. Long weekend, a few walks along the coast path, pint at the end of it. Lovely.
A: It is lovely. I've got a picture of the harbour on my wall, behind me.
B: I thought that looked familiar. Is that the one with all the coloured houses?
A: Yes, that's it. Sorry, I'm not very exciting to talk to. Is that alright?
B: You're doing grand, mate. Honestly, I'd take Tenby over Vegas half the time. Don't tell the lads I said
A: I won't.
